request.spec:
Claims can be selected (a checkbox on each) and opened together with one button. Each selected
claim that can be opened is opened and numbered in list order (the list order of people, newest
claim first within a person); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were opened and
how many were refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Claims can be selected (a checkbox on each) and opened together with one button. Each selected
claim that can be opened is opened and numbered in list order (the list order of people, newest
claim first within a person); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were opened and
how many were refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk open works: each claim now has a checkbox, and one "Open selected claims" button opens all the selected ones and shows how many were opened and how many were refused. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the bulk-open test (2 opened, 2 refused, numbered 2 and 3 in list order, audit lines match) and the three existing scenarios.

I only changed the front end; the server and stored data are untouched.

- **Checkbox per claim** (`claim-select`), in `features/claims/list.slot.tsx`. Which claims are ticked is kept in the URL (`selectedClaims`), as `DESIGN`/`useSearchParam` says to do for selected rows. Each tick works from the current URL, so several quick clicks don't lose each other.
- **Bulk-open panel**, in the new `features/claims/bulkopen.slot.tsx`: the `bulk-open` button, with the counts in `bulk-opened` and `bulk-refused`. It puts the selected claims in list order (people as listed, newest claim first within a person), then sends each one, one at a time, to the same open request the per-claim Open button uses. A claim that can't be opened, such as one already open or one dated in a closed period, is refused and left as it is. So the refusal rules and the audit lines (`CLAIM_OPENED` / `ROLLUP` / `TOTALS`) are exactly those of opening each claim by hand.
- **The counts** are cleared while it runs and shown once it's done. The selection is cleared afterwards.

Two behaviours you might not expect:
- **Not all-or-nothing.** Each claim is a separate request. If another user changes the sheet partway through, some claims may already be open when the rest are refused; the counts still report it correctly.
- **Hidden claims are skipped.** A selected claim whose person is currently hidden (a retired person with "Show retired" off) is not opened and isn't counted.
